title: Étale, affine pro-étale and weakly étale morphisms
statement:
Let $u\colon U\to X$ be a morphism of schemes.

1. If $u$ is étale, then $u$ is weakly étale [def-weil-weakly-etale-morphism].
2. If $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $u$ is affine pro-étale, i.e. $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$
   with $R\to B$ ind-étale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], then $u$ is weakly étale.
3. If $u$ is weakly étale and locally of finite presentation, then $u$ is étale.
4. On affine charts $U\supset\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X$, $u$ is
   weakly étale if and only if $R\to B$ and the multiplication $B\otimes_RB\to B$ are flat.

proof.text: Fix affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset U$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X$ with $u(V)\subset T$. The open-fibre-product lemma identifies $W=V\times_TV$ with the open $p_1^{-1}(V)\cap p_2^{-1}(V)$ of $U\times_XU$, and the affine fibre-product lemma identifies $W$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_RB)$, with the stated two inclusion maps on rings. Since $p_i\Delta_u=\mathrm{id}_U$, its inverse image is $\Delta_u^{-1}(W)=V$. Thus the restriction of $\Delta_u$ to these opens is $\Delta_{V/T}$; its ring map sends $b\otimes1$ and $1\otimes b$ to $b$, so is precisely multiplication $\mu:B\otimes_RB\to B$, $b\otimes c\mapsto bc$.

source.place: Tags 01JR (lemma-open-fibre-product), 01JQ (lemma-fibre-product-affines); the diagonal identified by the two projections

proof.text: Prove clause 4 with the conditions imposed on every such affine chart. The affine flatness criterion says that $u$ is flat exactly when every $R\to B$ is flat. By the affine-ring flatness equivalence, the restricted diagonal of step 1 is flat exactly when $\mu$ is flat. A point $v\in U$ has an affine chart $V\to T$ as above; its image $\Delta_u(v)$ lies in the open $W$ of step 1. Restricting source and target to open neighbourhoods leaves the two local rings and their induced homomorphism unchanged. Hence the stalk definition of flatness says that $\Delta_u$ is flat exactly when all these restricted diagonals are flat. Only a neighbourhood of each point in the image of the diagonal is needed; these particular $W$ need not cover the entire product. The definition of weakly etale now gives both implications of clause 4.

source.place: Tag 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize), applied to u and the affine restrictions of its diagonal

proof.text: For clause 1, the definition of etale gives flatness of $u$ and unramifiedness, and the definition of unramified gives that $\Delta_u$ is an open immersion. An open immersion identifies its source with an open subscheme, so its maps on local rings are isomorphisms; a ring is flat over itself (tensoring with it is the identity). Thus $\Delta_u$ is flat by the stalk definition. The two flatness conditions are exactly weak etaleness.

source.place: Tag 094X, lemma-when-weakly-etale, case (4), with the open-immersion flatness argument written out

proof.text: For clause 2, let $R\to B$ be the ind-etale map in the hypothesis. The ind-etale stability node states explicitly that an ind-etale map is weakly etale. In the ring terminology fixed in the ind-etale definition node this says that $R\to B$ and $B\otimes_RB\to B$ are flat. Apply the affine ring-map/flat-morphism equivalence to $R\to B$ to obtain flatness of $u$. Step 1 with $V=U$ and $T=X$ identifies its whole diagonal with $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_RB\to B)$, which is flat by the same equivalence. Thus the two conditions in the weakly etale definition hold. This proves weak etaleness of $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ without imposing any finiteness condition on the colimit.

source.place: Tag 097N, lemma-ind-etale-implies; use only the ind-etale-implies-weakly-etale clause of the existing stability node

proof.text: For clause 3, suppose $u$ is weakly etale and locally of finite presentation. For every chart $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\to T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ in step 1, the affine finite-presentation criterion gives $B=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(r_1,\ldots,r_m)$. Set $C=B\otimes_RB$ and let $I\subset C$ be the ideal generated by $x_i\otimes1-1\otimes x_i$ for $1\le i\le n$. Multiplication kills these generators and gives $\bar\mu:C/I\to B$. The map $b\mapsto[b\otimes1]$ is an inverse: in $C/I$ the two images of each algebra generator agree, so the two images of every $b\in B$ agree, and therefore $[b\otimes c]=[bc\otimes1]$. Hence $B\cong C/I$ as $C$-algebras. This is a finite presentation with zero algebra generators and $n$ relations. The calculation also applies when $n=0$.

source.place: Tag 0818, lemma-diagonal-morphism-finite-type, first conclusion; affine finite-generator calculation of the same conclusion

proof.text: The presentation in step 5 and the diagonal chart of step 1 give, around each $v\in U$, an affine source neighbourhood $V$ and affine target neighbourhood $W\ni\Delta_u(v)$ such that $V\to W$ is of finite presentation. This is exactly the definition of $\Delta_u$ being locally of finite presentation. The diagonal is also a monomorphism: if $\Delta_u\circ a=\Delta_u\circ b$, composition with $p_1$ gives $a=b$. Its flatness is part of the hypothesis that $u$ is weakly etale. Apply the flat locally finitely presented monomorphism leaf to $\Delta_u$ to obtain an open immersion.

source.place: Tag 025G, theorem-etale-radicial-open, (3) implies (1), applied to the diagonal

proof.text: Finally $u$ is locally of finite type: in every affine chart the finite presentation from step 5 supplies finitely many algebra generators, and these charts cover each inverse image of an affine base open. This is the definition of locally of finite type. Together with the open diagonal from step 6 it makes $u$ unramified. Since $u$ is also flat and locally of finite presentation by hypothesis, the definition of etale proves clause 3.

source.place: Tags 02GE (lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism), parts (2) and (3), and 02GV (lemma-flat-unramified-etale); the criteria recorded in the cited definition nodes
